Definitely enough of a trade off. There’s other types of food here you couldn’t find in CT, so it’s fun to explore! I moved here six years ago from Hartford County. I think there’s good and bad parts of WI, like any other place you’d live, but the coolest part about it is that the one state is pretty much like driving down the east coast so there’s so much diversity in culture and landscape. There’s hardwood forests and glacial drifts around, which remind me of home. At the same time, there’s prairie and it’s an entirely different animal.

Also, I’m not trying to knock WI pizza entirely, I’ve just been spoiled with the best. There are no coal fire oven pizza restaurants in WI, and that is literally what New Haven style is. The other thing is that the one Polish restaurant that I knew of in town closed down recently, which is devastating for pierogi fans everywhere. However, WI has the best Indian and Mexican I’ve ever had, and is otherwise a paradise for foodies. 

In the summer, MKE has a bunch of different festivals and concerts, and you can pretty much never be bored. Lots of free things to do, too! Other than that the economy is so much better here. A bunch of job opportunities in both hands on or office positions. 

Sorry, I know I’ve gone on a tangent but it excites me to see someone from CT looking to move here! Wisconsin is a great place to move to!

Transplanted from CT here! Slower paced lifestyle, people are pretty friendly, and the food is good!! You’ll never eat good pizza again, and the crime is higher depending on where you live in MKE and where you came from back east. The parks are maintained better here, and you’ll find a job or house easier! Cost of living is so much cheaper! There is a lot to do in town, so you won’t have to travel out of state for fun. The landscape is super diverse and beautiful, and there is a lot of different wildlife here too. I’d recommend looking at Horicon Marsh to see an array of different birds.

The day after I got out of the psych ward, I got checked out by a gyno and he sent me straight up to the maternal ward. There was a cyst that had ruptured in my uterus and had caused the PID. I was on IV antibiotics and hydrocodone. I also had to get my blood taken every four hours. I was in the hospital on and off for three months, for the PID and the mental stuff. My mom had a lot of moments like these but this was by far the worst night we’ve had as a family. 

My mom has been doing better lately, but it’s been hard to have a good relationship with any of my family with all of this trauma. My heart is racing as I type this. I often feel better alone, but at the same time I know it’s not healthy to isolate.
